items.summary: No schema, migrations or models exist in the repo; server.js:16 and :35 imply users and invoices tables, and :30 a reset_token column. Passwords are stored in the user-level 'password' column and invoices are fetched with no owner column visible.
items.fix: Define the schema in a migration tool with primary and foreign keys, NOT NULL, a unique index on normalised email, and an owner/tenant column on invoices.

items.summary: No migration tool, migration files or CI exist. server.js requires ./db, which is not in the repo.
evidence: searched: migrations|knex|prisma|flyway|alembic and .github workflows across repo
items.fix: Adopt a migration tool (Knex, Prisma Migrate or node-pg-migrate), commit versioned migrations, and run them in the deploy pipeline.

items.summary: No schema is in the repo, so indexes cannot be matched to queries. Queries filter users by email (server.js:23, :30) and invoices by id (:35).
items.question: Show the production schema (pg_dump --schema-only or equivalent) so indexes on users.email and invoices can be checked.

items.summary: No N+1 loops, but GET /invoices/:id returns a single row so unbounded sets are not present yet. There are no list endpoints at all, so this is mostly untested territory.
items.fix: When list endpoints are added, apply LIMIT and a max page size from the start.

items.summary: Connection pooling and timeouts cannot be seen: ./db is missing from the repo and server.js sets no pool settings.
items.fix: Configure a pool with explicit max size and timeouts in the db module, and use a provider pooler if deployed serverless or multi-instance.

items.summary: No IaC or backup config in the repo; the database host is not identifiable.
items.question: Show the managed database backup setting (console screenshot or IaC) with frequency and retention.

items.summary: No restore runbook or drill record in the repo.
evidence: searched: restore|runbook|disaster|recovery in README.md and docs
items.question: Show a dated restore drill record with timing and written steps, or confirm none has been done.

items.summary: No server-side validation on any write path: /signup, /login, /forgot and /charge use req.body fields directly with no schema, type, length or range limits. /charge takes price and qty from the client and an undefined password would throw in createHash.
items.fix: Add zod (or Joi) validation at every handler: email format and length, password length, qty as a bounded positive integer; have the server look up the price by product id (stripe playbook ST-2).

items.summary: No schema or timestamp columns are visible, and no date handling or scheduled work exists in server.js.
items.question: Show the production schema to confirm timestamps use timestamptz (UTC).

items.summary: All SQL is built by string interpolation of user input (apostrophes in an email or id break or inject into the query), and charset of the database is unknown.
items.fix: Use parameterised queries ($1 placeholders) everywhere, and confirm the database encoding is UTF-8. Treat the injection itself as urgent; a human engineer should review all queries.

items.summary: Money is computed with floats: price * qty * 1.0825 then Math.round(total * 100), with price and qty taken from the request body and currency hardcoded to usd with no currency column. Stripe playbook ST-2 and ST-9 apply.
items.fix: Store and compute prices as integer minor units with an explicit currency; look up the price server-side by product or Stripe Price id, and round tax in one documented step (or use Stripe Tax).

items.summary: There are no list endpoints in the app yet, so pagination does not apply to current code.
